title: Deconstructing Multi-Step Geometric Transformations
originalTopic: Graph Transformations: Scaling, Reflecting, and Shifting
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe how the graph of y = 1 - 2*sqrt(x + 3) is obtained from the standard base graph of y = sqrt(x) through a sequence of geometric transformations.
finalAnswer: Shift left 3 units, stretch vertically by factor 2, reflect across x-axis, shift up 1 unit.

steps.title: Start with the Elementary Function
steps.explanation: Identify the base parent function y_0 = sqrt(x), which has endpoint at (0,0) and domain [0, inf).
steps.why: All transformation sequences begin by identifying the elementary parent curve.

steps.title: Apply Horizontal Shift
steps.explanation: Replacing x with x + 3 translates the graph 3 units to the left, shifting the starting endpoint to (-3, 0).
steps.why: f(x + c) shifts the graph leftward by c units for c > 0.

steps.title: Apply Vertical Stretch and Reflection
steps.explanation: Multiplying by 2 stretches the graph vertically away from the x-axis by a factor of 2. The negative sign reflects the curve across the x-axis, causing it to open downward.
steps.why: -c*f(x) stretches by c and reflects over the horizontal axis.

steps.title: Apply Vertical Shift
steps.explanation: Adding 1 shifts the entire curve upward by 1 unit, placing the new endpoint at (-3, 1). The range becomes (-inf, 1].
steps.why: Adding a constant to the outer expression shifts the curve vertically.
